title: Open a glass studio (hot shop, cold shop, classes, optional cafe or events) in Albemarle County: the master path and decision points
question: I want to open a glassblowing studio in Albemarle County with a gas-fired furnace, glory hole, kilns and torches, teach classes to the public, and maybe run a small cafe or sip-and-blow events. Which County and state approvals do I need, in what order, and who do I talk to first?
office: Community Development Department (Planning, Zoning, Building Inspections and Engineering, with a free pre-application meeting as the front door); Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Community Risk & Resilience (Fire Marshal's Office); Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration; Blue Ridge Health District (Virginia Department of Health) for food; Albemarle County Service Authority for public water and sewer
summary: A glass studio in Albemarle County is several approvals stacked together. First settle the site: the use must be allowed in the parcel's zoning district (industrial districts allow manufacturing by right; commercial districts allow retail and instruction; the Rural Areas allow only limited home occupations and uses by special use permit), and any new or changed commercial use needs a Zoning Clearance before a building permit or sign permit, and an approved site plan for a new building. Book the free Monday pre-application meeting with Community Development to confirm the use, the district, and whether a special use permit, site plan or Architectural Review Board review is needed. Then: commercial building, mechanical (fuel gas), electrical and plumbing permits in Civic Access for the furnace, glory hole, kilns, exhaust and gas piping, ending in a certificate of occupancy; the Fire Marshal's operational permits under the Statewide Fire Prevention Code (hot work, compressed gases including oxygen, LP-gas, industrial ovens, and a place of assembly if more than 50 people gather); a County business license from the Department of Finance & Budget (the county has no Commissioner of the Revenue) plus the business tangible personal property or machinery and tools return; a sign permit; and, if you serve food or drink, a Blue Ridge Health District food establishment permit, the County's 6% food and beverage tax, and a Virginia ABC license. Water, sewer, grease, propane or natural gas, stormwater and air rules are the last layer. Each piece has its own process file (glass_studio_zoning_use, glass_studio_building_mechanical, glass_studio_fire_permits, glass_studio_business_license, glass_studio_food_and_events, glass_studio_utilities_and_environment).

steps.step: Decide what kind of studio you are opening, because the answer sets the path
steps.who: You (the owner), ideally with your architect or mechanical contractor
steps.how: Four decisions drive everything else. (1) Use: a hot shop with a gas-fired furnace, glory hole and kilns is a manufacturing or fabrication use under the Zoning Ordinance and a factory-type occupancy under the building code; a studio that mostly sells finished work and teaches classes is retail and instruction; a demonstration or class space where the public gathers can be an assembly use. (2) Place: a Light Industry (LI) or Heavy Industry (HI) parcel in the Development Areas allows manufacturing by right; commercial districts (C-1, CO, HC, PD-SC, DCD and the like) allow retail and teaching but may not allow the furnace work; the Rural Areas (RA) allow only a home occupation of limited size and trips, with anything larger needing a special use permit. (3) Cafe or not: serving prepared food or drink adds a Blue Ridge Health District food establishment permit, the County's 6% food and beverage tax, grease-trap and plumbing rules, and possibly a fire 'open flames and candles' permit for dining areas. (4) Alcohol or not: sip-and-blow events need a Virginia ABC license (a retail wine and beer or mixed beverage license for a regular bar, or a banquet license per event) and the County's ABC flat-fee license line. Write these answers down; they are what the pre-application meeting will ask.
steps.basis: Albemarle County Code Chapter 18 (Zoning Ordinance) districts and use tables (Municode, not reprinted); 13VAC5-63 (USBC); 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC Table 107.2); Va. Code § 58.1-3833; Va. Code § 4.1-206.3
steps.paraphrase: The pre-application meeting exists so that the applicant and County staff share one understanding of the project.

steps.step: Look up the parcel's zoning district and overlays before you sign a lease
steps.who: You; Community Development zoning staff on request
steps.how: Use the County GIS-Web viewer to find the parcel's zoning district, whether it is in the Development Areas or the Rural Areas, and whether it lies in an Entrance Corridor overlay (Architectural Review Board review of buildings, signs and equipment), a floodplain or steep-slope area, or the Albemarle County Service Authority jurisdictional area for public water and sewer. If the use's classification is unclear, ask the Zoning Administrator for a written Letter of Determination ($220 plus 4%; may take up to 90 days) or ask at the pre-application meeting first. The glass_studio_zoning_use file walks through districts, home occupations and special use permits.
steps.fee: Official Letter of Determination: $220 plus the 4% technology surcharge (optional)
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Determinations and Appeals page (Internet Archive copy of 12 May 2026); Community Development fee schedule
steps.paraphrase: A Letter of Determination takes staff research and can take up to 90 days.

steps.step: Book the free Monday pre-application meeting with Community Development
steps.who: You; the Community Development pre-application coordinator (cdd-preapps@albemarle.org, 434-296-5832); Planning, Zoning and Engineering staff, with VDOT, the Albemarle County Service Authority and Fire Rescue invited when relevant
steps.how: Email or call the pre-application coordinator to describe the project; staff decide whether the meeting is 'mandatory' (required before a special use permit or zoning map amendment) or 'exploratory' (site plans, zoning clearances and general questions). Register in Civic Access, choose Request, then Pre-Application Meeting, and file the request. Send the completed request and a conceptual sketch plan (parcel, entrance, building or area to be used, parking, streams, slopes, floodplain) to the coordinator by 12 noon on a Monday; meetings are held Mondays at 2, 3 or 4 pm by Microsoft Teams and are scheduled no later than noon on the Monday before. There is no fee. Ask specifically about: use classification and district; whether a special use permit, special exception or zoning map amendment is needed; site plan or site plan amendment; Entrance Corridor review; water and sewer; fire access and the Fire Marshal's permits for furnaces, oxygen and propane; and stormwater.
steps.deadline: Request and sketch plan by 12 pm on a Monday; a mandatory meeting is scheduled within two weeks and cannot take place until at least two weeks before an official submittal deadline
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Pre-Application Meeting page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026)
steps.paraphrase: Meetings run on Mondays at 2, 3 or 4 pm (not on holidays) and cost nothing.

steps.step: Get the zoning approvals: Zoning Clearance, and any special use permit, special exception or site plan
steps.who: You or your agent; Community Development Zoning and Planning; the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors for special use permits
steps.how: Every new commercial or industrial business needs a Zoning Clearance ($60 plus 4% for a business in commercial or industrial space; $30 plus 4% for a home occupation) filed in Civic Access, and it must be approved before a tenant up-fit building permit or any sign permit is issued. A new building or a change to the approved site layout needs a site development plan (initial site plan $1,775 plus 4%; minor amendment $590 plus 4%). A use that the district lists only by special use permit goes to a public hearing before the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors ($2,365 plus 4% plus the $235 notice base fee; a Class B home occupation in a residential district is $1,185 plus 4%). Details, districts and timing are in glass_studio_zoning_use.
steps.deadline: Zoning Clearance before the building permit for a tenant up-fit and before any sign permit; special use permits follow the County's SP/ZMA submittal schedule
steps.fee: Zoning Clearance, all other uses: $60 plus 4%; Special Use Permit, all other: $2,365 plus 4%; Initial Site Plan: $1,775 plus 4% (see fees)
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Commercial Building Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 16 March 2026); Community Development fee schedule (Internet Archive copy of 20 August 2026)
steps.paraphrase: A new tenant fitting out space must have an approved Zoning Clearance before the building permit is issued.

steps.step: Get the building, mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fuel-gas permits, then the certificate of occupancy
steps.who: Your licensed contractors (each trade applies for its own sub-permit); Community Development Building Inspections
steps.how: Apply in Civic Access for the commercial building permit (new building, addition or Commercial Alteration for a tenant up-fit; a Change in Building Occupancy Classification if the space was something else) with building plans, a life-safety plan, the approved site plan and, for a new building, VDOT approval. Mechanical (furnace, glory hole, kilns, exhaust hoods and make-up air, gas piping), electrical and plumbing work are separate sub-permits. Inspections are requested in Civic Access; the certificate of occupancy comes after the final inspections, and the Health Department will not issue a food permit for a new or remodeled space until the certificate of occupancy exists. Details and fees are in glass_studio_building_mechanical.
steps.deadline: Permits before work starts; the certificate of occupancy before the space is occupied or used
steps.fee: New commercial building: $0.24 per sq. ft. up to 5,000 sq. ft. plus $0.17 per sq. ft. over 5,000, minimum $90; alterations: $0.20 per sq. ft., minimum $90; mechanical new commercial: $0.04 per sq. ft., minimum $90; gas or oil lines: $40; plus plan review rows and the 4% surcharge (see glass_studio_building_mechanical)
steps.basis: 13VAC5-63-80 (USBC § 108.1); Albemarle County Community Development, Application Requirements page (Internet Archive copy of 13 August 2026)
steps.paraphrase: Each trade (electrical, plumbing, mechanical, gas, fire alarm, sprinkler) files its own permit application where it applies.

steps.step: Get the Fire Marshal's operational permits before you fire the furnace or store gases
steps.who: You; Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Community Risk & Resilience (Fire Marshal's Office)
steps.how: Albemarle enforces the Statewide Fire Prevention Code and charges for operational permits under its Fire Marshal fee schedule (effective January 19, 2022). A hot shop will usually need: hot work (fixed-site equipment such as a glory hole or torch bench), compressed gas (oxygen above 504 cubic feet, flammable gas above 200 cubic feet), LP-gas if propane is stored or used, industrial ovens (fuel-fired furnaces and kilns regulated by IFC Chapter 30), and a place of assembly permit if more than 50 people gather for classes, demonstrations or events. Most are $200 a year per location, with a facility inspection (first two hours free, then $100 an hour) and $100 re-inspections if violations are not corrected. Apply on the Fire Prevention Permit Application (General) web form. Details are in glass_studio_fire_permits.
steps.deadline: Before the activity starts; annual permits renew by the inspection anniversary date
steps.fee: Typically $200 per permit per year per location; facility inspection free for the first two hours, then $100 per hour; re-inspection $100 (see glass_studio_fire_permits)
steps.basis: 13VAC5-52-70 (SFPC § 107.2 and Table 107.2); Albemarle County Fire Rescue, Permits & Inspections page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026) and Fire Marshal fee schedule (Internet Archive copy of 15 May 2026)
steps.paraphrase: The Fire Rescue Community Risk & Resilience section issues the fire permits and does the inspections, covering hazardous materials, places of assembly, tents, burning and more.

steps.step: Get the County business license and file the business property return
steps.who: You; Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit)
steps.how: After zoning approval, send the New Business License Application to the Office of Revenue Administration by email or mail (there is no online account opening for a new business). Under $25,000 in gross receipts there is no fee but you still file; $25,000 to under $100,000 is a $50 fee; at $100,000 and above the tax is by classification (retail $0.20 per $100; repair, personal, business and other services $0.36 per $100). Report furnaces, kilns, tools, furniture and fixtures on the Business Tangible Personal Property return by May 1 each year ($4.28 per $100 of assessed value); if the County classifies the studio as a manufacturer, the production equipment is reported separately as machinery and tools at the same rate. Details are in glass_studio_business_license.
steps.deadline: License before opening (the County form allows 30 days from the start date; state law says before starting); BTPP return by May 1 each year; renewals by March 1
steps.fee: License: $0 under $25,000; $50 from $25,000 to under $100,000; rate-based at $100,000 and above
steps.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3700; Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Start a Business page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026)
steps.paraphrase: A new business goes to Community Development for zoning approval and to the Department of Finance for its license.

steps.step: If you will serve food or drink: Health District permit, food and beverage tax, and ABC license
steps.who: You; Blue Ridge Health District Environmental Health (Charlottesville/Albemarle office); Office of Revenue Administration; Virginia ABC
steps.how: Submit the Health District's plan review application and food establishment permit application at least 30 days before opening or starting renovation and before construction begins ($40 plan review, $40 annual permit); pass the pre-opening inspection after the certificate of occupancy is issued. Register with the County for the 6% food and beverage tax, remitted by the 20th of each month. For wine, beer or spirits at sip-and-blow events, apply to Virginia ABC (application fee $195 per license plus the annual state license tax, for example $450 for an on-and-off-premises wine and beer license, or a banquet license per event), and pay the County's ABC flat-fee license line (for example beer and wine on premises $37.50 a year). One-off food at events uses a temporary food establishment permit ($40). Details are in glass_studio_food_and_events.
steps.deadline: Health District applications at least 30 days before opening; food and beverage tax returns by the 20th monthly
steps.fee: Health District: $40 plan review, $40 annual permit, $40 temporary event; ABC application $195 plus annual tax; County ABC flat fee by license type
steps.basis: Va. Code § 35.1-18; 12VAC5-421-3660; Va. Code § 58.1-3833; Va. Code § 4.1-230(C); Albemarle County Finance & Budget, Food & Beverage Tax page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026)
steps.paraphrase: A business that prepares and serves food or drink collects the County's food and beverage tax and pays it over by the 20th of the following month.

steps.step: Arrange water, sewer, grease control, fuel supply, stormwater and air clearance
steps.who: You; Albemarle County Service Authority; Columbia Gas of Virginia or a propane supplier; Community Development Engineering; Virginia DEQ
steps.how: If the parcel is in the ACSA jurisdictional area, ACSA sets water and sewer connection and capacity charges, requires a signed building permit before scheduling a meter, and requires a Fats, Oils and Grease collection device and FOG permit for food service; outside the area you are on well and septic through the Health District. Natural gas comes from the utility where mains exist; otherwise plan a propane tank and the Fire Marshal's LP-gas permit. that disturb over 10,000 square feet, or building on a site that needs grading, triggers the County's land disturbance (VESMP) plan review and permit. A gas-fired glass furnace or kiln under 50,000,000 Btu per hour is exempt from a DEQ minor new source review permit as fuel-burning equipment, but a facility's total uncontrolled emissions must stay under the exemption table, so keep burner ratings and fuel use on file. Details are in glass_studio_utilities_and_environment.
steps.deadline: Before construction (ACSA plans, land disturbance) and before opening (FOG permit, gas service)
steps.fee: ACSA system development and RWSA capacity charges by meter size (see ACSA); land disturbance under 1 acre: $235 plus 4%, 1 to 5 acres: $2,205 plus 4% (County fee schedule)
steps.basis: Va. Code § 62.1-44.15:34(A); 9VAC5-80-1105(B)(1); Albemarle County Service Authority, Start or Stop Service page (Internet Archive copy of 15 May 2026)
steps.quote: We require at least a signed building permit before we can schedule meter installation.

steps.step: Order the sign permit, open, and keep the annual renewals
steps.how: A sign permit (temporary $30 plus 4%; permanent needing Architectural Review Board sign review $140 plus 4%; electric sign trade permit $55) is issued only after the Zoning Clearance. Then open. Each year: renew the business license by March 1, file the BTPP or machinery and tools return by May 1, renew the Fire Marshal's operational permits and pass the annual inspection by the anniversary date, renew the Health District food permit (annual, not transferable), remit food and beverage tax monthly, and renew the ABC license. Keep every permit posted or on the premises.
steps.deadline: Business license renewal March 1; BTPP return May 1; fire permits and Health permit annually
steps.fee: Sign permits: $30 or $140 plus 4%; Electric - Signs: $55
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Sign Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 17 April 2026); Community Development fee schedule
steps.paraphrase: A sign needs its own permit, separate from the permit for the use itself.

escalation.trigger: Zoning staff say the studio is not an allowed use, or you disagree with a Zoning Administrator determination or Zoning Clearance decision
escalation.next: Appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals (notice of appeal filed with the zoning administrator and the board), or apply for a special use permit, special exception or zoning map amendment instead
escalation.deadline: 30 days after the decision (10 days for decisions on temporary or seasonal commercial uses)
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 15.2-2311(A); Albemarle County Determinations and Appeals page; Community Development fee schedule (Appeal, Board of Zoning Appeals, $350 plus 4%)
escalation.quote: The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.

escalation.trigger: A building code decision you disagree with (permit refused, failed inspection, refused modification, refused certificate of occupancy)
escalation.next: Albemarle County Board of Building Code Appeals ($350 plus 4%), then the State Building Code Technical Review Board, then circuit court
escalation.deadline: Written appeal within 30 calendar days of receiving the decision; State Review Board within 21 calendar days of the local board's decision
escalation.quote: Any person aggrieved by the local building department's application of the Building Code or refusal to grant a modification to the provisions of the Building Code may appeal to the local board of Building Code appeals.

escalation.trigger: A fire official's decision you disagree with (permit conditions, refused modification, inspection order)
escalation.next: Local Board of Fire Prevention Code Appeals (the Fire Marshal's fee schedule lists a $350 application fee for a Fire Code Board of Appeals request), then the State Building Code Technical Review Board
escalation.deadline: Within 14 calendar days of the application of the SFPC; State Review Board within 21 calendar days of receipt of the local board's decision
escalation.quote: The appeal shall be submitted to the LBFPCA within 14 calendar days of the application of the SFPC.

escalation.trigger: You disagree with a business license classification or assessment
escalation.next: Written appeal to the Director of Finance (local administrative appeal under the BPOL statute), then the Virginia Tax Commissioner, then circuit court
escalation.deadline: Within one year of the assessment (local appeal); 90 days from the local determination to the Tax Commissioner
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(5); see bpol_business_license for the full route
escalation.quote: Any person assessed with a local license tax as a result of an appealable event as defined in this section may file an administrative appeal of the assessment within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of the appealable event, whichever is later, with the commissioner of the revenue or other local assessing official.

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers (HTTP 403), so every County page and PDF cited here was read from its newest Internet Archive capture; the capture dates are in the sources. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content, so County quotes are kept short and each carries a paraphrase; the published page should show the paraphrase and the link, not the County's words.

The Zoning Ordinance (County Code Chapter 18) is published on Municode, whose terms forbid automated access and republication. The district and use statements in this file (industrial districts allow manufacturing by right; commercial districts allow retail and instruction; the Rural Areas allow home occupations and listed special uses) are a summary for orientation, not a reading of the current use tables, and must be confirmed on Municode or with zoning staff. The exact use name the County applies to a hot glass studio (manufacturing, artisan or craft production, or retail with accessory fabrication) was not found on any County page and is an office question.

Fees are from the Community Development fee schedule capture of 20 August 2026 and the Fire Marshal fee schedule effective January 19, 2022. The Board of Supervisors adopted a revised Community Development fee schedule on April 22, 2026, effective January 1, 2027 (see the building_permit_residential and short_term_rental_registration files); amounts for 2027 were not read here.

The Fire Marshal's fee schedule PDF is a scanned table whose columns do not read cleanly in text; the $200 annual figure for industrial ovens, LP-gas, compressed gas and places of assembly and the $100 cutting-and-welding figure follow the PDF's reading order and should be confirmed with the Fire Marshal's Office.

Privacy: County and Health District pages name individual staff (pre-application coordinator, planners, zoning administrators, a fire permits contact). Only office lines and role mailboxes are recorded here.
The Civic Access portal, the Fire Rescue web forms, the ACSA service request form and the ABC licensing portal were not opened; no account was created and nothing was submitted.

abc.virginia.gov and deq.virginia.gov refuse automated requests and their newest Internet Archive copies are from 2023; the ABC and DEQ statements here rest on the Code of Virginia and the Virginia Administrative Code rather than agency pages.

Whether the studio is a 'manufacturer' for machinery and tools tax purposes, whether classes make part of the space an assembly occupancy, and which Fire Marshal permits apply to a particular furnace and gas set-up are decisions the County makes case by case; they are listed as open questions.
